Comments: On April 13 2023, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Wafra INC 1 OG Well. Accompany's in today's inspection was Matt Wood (DEP OGI)The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspection, the well appeared to be equipped for production. The well tag was present at the time of the inspection.The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. There were no erosion or sedimentation issues onsite. There were observed leaks and discharge on the ground and around the wellhead. The Department observed the pump jack releasing a fluid to the ground. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the area as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The Department requests the operator provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. Soil and water conductivity readings were taken at the site of the stained soil and water coming out of the wellhead. The soil conductivity reading was 1.10ms and the water reading was 2.44mS. The Operator (James Stifler from Apollo) was informed of the situation via telephone. Bases on today's inspection violations will be issued at this time.

Violation ID: 976204
Permit API: 131-20531
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Windham Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial/Aerial Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/10/2022
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build-Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on both wells on the DeWolf pad, the Evelyn Wyo. 4H and the Evelyn Wyo. 2H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess recent remedial work of Perf. and Squeeze Ops. The Evelyn Wyo. 4H wells Conductor x Surface (20"x 13 3/8") annulus has an open casing top in cellar, the Evelyn Wyo. 2H Conductor by Surface (20" x13 3/8") annulus is capped and set up for venting to atmosphere via a 1" pipe to surface and a Sentry valve (Sentry replaced with bull plug for testing). Both wells remained in production through the SPBUT period. All annuli of each well have been shut in for testing. The (20"x13") annulus was shut in for 72hrs., the (13"x9") annuli were shut in for 48hrs. and the (9"x5") annuli were shut in for 24hrs. resulting in SPBUTs. - Upon arrival it was noted the cellar of the 4H was bubbling. I met with CALLC Field Rep. (Denny DeWolf) and Creston Consultant Reps. (Jason Rajan and Dakota Manning). Lease operator turned the valve on the non monitored side of the well head in the cellar and the bubbling slowed down. During testing and sampling of the 4H, once the (13x9) annulus was open and venting to production tank, the bubbling stopped. A water truck was scheduled to remove water in cellar in order to grease the valves. - Starting at approx. 10:35 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter (cal. 11/10/22). Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for both of the Evelyn Wyo. wells on this pad: - Evelyn Wyo 4H: - (20x13): open casing top in cellar, no bubbling noted * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 3 psi.; 67% gas; Sample taken @ 10:40 - (9x5): 288 psi.; 76% gas; Sample taken @ 10:45 - Evelyn Wyo. 2H: - (20x13): 0 psi.; 80% gas; Sample taken @ 10:55 * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 7.0 psi.; 67% gas; Sample taken @ 11:00 - (9x5); 122 psi.; 80% gas; Sample taken @ 11:02 - All annuli were returned to venting by 11:05

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/02/2026 to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Township, Bradford county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/02/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8269681
Permit API: 015-24012
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/02/2026
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Lee North well pad (1H expansion) located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/2/2026 at 1025 hours. The weather was 44 degrees F with cloudy skies and light rain. A Blackhill Energy representative accompanied me during the inspection. On 3/6/2026, the DEP noted violations due to sediment laden fluids having been observed escaping the site's limit-of-disturbance (LOD) and impacting Wetland 4J located downslope of the stormwater control basin's outlet pipe. Additional information regarding the inspection from 3/6/2026 can be seen in inspection record #4154382. Blackhill Energy responded to the violations noted on 3/6/2026 by having the construction contractor install additional filter sock around the outlet pipe. The additional controls were installed within a few hours of the DEP notifying Blackhill Energy of the findings. On 3/9/2026, the construction contractor returned and installed a rock outlet apron and additional filtration measures around the discharge point. During this inspection, recent rainfall has added additional sediment laden fluids into the stormwater control basin. The skimmer pipe that flows fluids from the basin into the outlet box was not functioning as designed (photo #6). As seen in photo #6, sediment laden fluids were directly entering the outlet box from around the skimmer pipe. The controls added below the basin's outlet pipe were observed to be overtopping with sediment laden fluids (photos #5, 7 and 9). The sediment laden fluids were observed escaping the site's LOD and entering wetland 4J (photo #8). A representative with the construction contractor took a look at the skimmer outlet pipe and explained that they could try to temporarily grout around the pipe within the outlet box to prevent fluids from entering the box before going through the skimmer. The construction contractor and Blackhill Energy both explained that additional controls would be added to the area below the basin's outlet pipe to help contain sediment laden fluids to the well site.Based on the findings of this inspection report and the continued release of sediment laden fluids outside of the site's LOD and into Wetland 4J, the violations cited against API #015-24012 on 3/6/2026 remain outstanding at this time.I departed the site at 1200 hours.

Violation ID: 960309
Permit API: 059-28088
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Springhill Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/23/2022
Comments: The Department conducted an inspection of the EQT Lumber 13H well on 6/23/2022. Hydraulic fracturing crews are on site. EQT stopped stimulation activities on the Lumber 13H after a landowner notified the operator of a communication incident on 6/19/2022. The Department became aware of the communication incident on 6/20/2022 and Department personnel responded to the incident. Based on the Departments investigation, the Department has determined the following. EQT was notified by the landowner on 6/19/2022 of the communication incident. EQT investigated and determined hydraulic fracturing operations at the Lumber well site communicated to an offset well. EQT personnel observed fluid and gas expressing from the offset well. EQT stopped stimulation activities on the Lumber 13H and the fluid and gas observations at the offset well subsided. Stimulation operations began on the Lumber 13H well on 5/29/2022. The offset well is approximately 6500 feet from the EQT Lumber 13H well. Prior to stopping stimulation activities, EQT completed 99 of 141 planned stages on the Lumber 13H well. Stage 100 is perforated but not completed on the Lumber 13H well. The offset well is approximately 3200 feet from stages 99 and 100 of the Lumber 13H well. Stages 99 and 100 are approximately 7820 TVD from ground level. Pursuant to 25 Pa. Code Section 78a.73, unconventional operators who are stimulating wells by way of hydraulic fracturing are required to notify the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) upon confirmation of a hydraulic fracturing communication incident. EQT did not notify the Department of the communication incident. A violation of 78a.73(c). Following notification, Technical Guidance Document (TGD) 800-0810-001, Guidelines for Implementing Area of Review (AOR) Regulatory Requirement for Unconventional Wells, describes the incident report that should be electronically filed within 3 days of the incident. The Department has not received the Area of Review Fracturing Communication Incident Report. The Department requests EQT to submit the incident report. At the time of the communication event, EQT was hydraulically fracturing multiple wells (1H, 5H, 13H, 15H) simultaneously. EQT continued hydraulic fracturing operations on an adjacent well (Lumber 11H) after the communication incident was confirmed. A violation of 78a.73(c). The Department requested EQT cease all hydraulic fracturing operations on June 21, 2022. EQT stopped hydraulic fracturing operations at the Lumber well site on 6/22/2022 at approximately 0900. Offset well information The total depth or well construction of the offset well is not known. The well is not identified. The offset well appears to be an abandoned unregistered well. At the offset well, the Department observed a sinkhole approximately 2 feet in diameter and 11.5 feet deep. In the sinkhole Department personnel observed 6-inch casing, 4-inch thin walled casing, and wooden conductor fragments in the sinkhole. A tire was also observed. The sinkhole appears to have washed out areas. 2 3/8" tubing appears to be coupled to the top of the 6-inch casing and extends approximately 30-inches above grade. Immediately adjacent to the appears to be the remnant production line. Department personnel checked the offset well and associated above ground piping for the presence of gas on the dates listed below. 6/20/2022 --sinkhole = 19% LEL. 2 3/8" tubing on 6-inch casing = No detections. 2 3/8" production line = no detections. 6/21/2022 --sinkhole = 100 ppm methane. 2 3/8" tubing on 6-inch casing = No detections. 2 3/8" production line = no detections. 6/23/2022 --sinkhole = No detections. 2 3/8" tubing on 6-inch casing = No detections. 2 3/8" production line = no detections. EQT has installed orange fencing around the offset well. A LEL monitor has been set up adjacent to the offset well. The Departments investigation is ongoing.

I informed the company man about the puddle before leaving the location and he said that he would have it removed immediately. No other issues noted. Outstanding violations noted.

Violation ID: 8212373
Permit API: 083-51666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/31/2024
Comments: Upon being made aware of a crude oil release near this conventional well, I contacted Pennhills and learned that a steel gathering line located along the eastern side of the road (downslope of this well) was found to be compromised on December 9, 2024 and actions were taken to repair the line and remediate impacted media at that time. Since that time, Pennhills has decommissioned and vac'd out all fluid from the compromised line and are currently using a different gathering line that parallels the western edge of the road to carry fluids from this well and others located beyond this location. Representatives of Pennhills stated that the bulk of the earth disturbance along the eastern edge of the road was conducted to locate the portion of the line that was leaking and that they constructed an underflow dam downslope of the road to contain residual product that continues to leach from the road bank due to the abundance of larger rocks and roots in the area. Upon my arrival for this inspection, I observed the disturbed area along the eastern edge of the road that accesses this well. There was no visual evidence of crude oil across this disturbance, which was temporarily stabilized with seed and mulch. Downslope of the road, an approximate 20'x30' area had soil exposed due to Pennhills' reported removal of oil soaked leaves from the area. Isolated pockets of crude oil remain throughout this area, which drains towards the underflow dam that is located approximately 100' east of the well [41.82619 -78.85691]. The underflow dam is functioning and appears to be regularly maintained, as there is currently only a minor sheen atop the standing water behind it.Crude oil was also observed on the surface at a recessed area approximately 30' east (41.82632 -78.85674 [downslope]) of the underflow dam that appears to have migrated subsurface from the vicinity of the underflow dam to this point.A second area of oil soaked leaves/soil was discovered approximately 30' south (41.82607 -78.85661) of the underflow dam in a currently dry channel.At this time, the constructed underflow dam and continued use of absorbent diapers/booms appear to be sufficient containment measures. It is highly suggested to regularly monitor the containment and evaluate downslope of the impacted area, particularly during and after rain and snowmelt events.The quantity of product released was unknown, but appears to be less than one barrel at this time. No watercourses have impacted by this incident at this time. Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate if the current containment remains sufficient, if there was further migration of crude oil or evidence is presented that indicates the released quantity was greater than one barrel.

Downslope of the road, an approximate 20'x30' area had soil exposed due to Pennhills' reported removal of oil soaked leaves from the area. Isolated pockets of crude oil remain throughout this area, which drains towards the underflow dam that is located approximately 100' east of the well [41.82619 -78.85691]. The underflow dam is functioning and appears to be regularly maintained, as there is currently only a minor sheen atop the standing water behind it.Crude oil was also observed on the surface at a recessed area approximately 30' east (41.82632 -78.85674 [downslope]) of the underflow dam that appears to have migrated subsurface from the vicinity of the underflow dam to this point.A second area of oil soaked leaves/soil was discovered approximately 30' south (41.82607 -78.85661) of the underflow dam in a currently dry channel.At this time, the constructed underflow dam and continued use of absorbent diapers/booms appear to be sufficient containment measures. It is highly suggested to regularly monitor the containment and evaluate downslope of the impacted area, particularly during and after rain and snowmelt events.The quantity of product released was unknown, but appears to be less than one barrel at this time. No watercourses have impacted by this incident at this time. Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate if the current containment remains sufficient, if there was further migration of crude oil or evidence is presented that indicates the released quantity was greater than one barrel.

Violation ID: 978546
Permit API: 035-21329
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/13/2022
Comments: On December 13, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline, John Ciccone, and Amber Boyd conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. At the time of inspection, the recently stimulated wells were in flow back. This inspection is to follow up with the multiple spills at this site. About half of the containment from the recent stimulation process has been removed. With the removal of some of the containment STL was able to excavate the area of elevated conductivity off the east end of the containment found on October 24, 2022. The area of excavation was about 90 ft. x 45 ft. and about 8 to 12 inches deep. The second area of elevated conductivity has been excavated to the containment. Containment remains in this area for the flow back process. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources was onsite and said STL Resources plans to continue the investigation of the extent of this spill area once the containment has been removed. The top layer of soil has been removed in this area adjacent to the containment in about a 10 ft. x 10 ft. area. Soil conductivity could not be screened in either of the excavated areas due to the ground being frozen.The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of thewell pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being hauled off site or pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in the northwest stormwater vault. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The hole in the well pad trench liner near the northwest stormwater vault has been fixed. Two patches have been added to the trench liner. The soil in the area where the water from the seep had been pooling up has been excavated and removed. A small berm has been built in the area and a tarp has been dug in to collect stormwater. This area is being vacuumed as necessary. The DEP screened the pooled water on the downgradient side of the built berm and the conductivity was 365 uS/cm. An area to the south of the area impacted from the seep of the northwest stormwater vault that had been previously excavated to remove contaminated soil from the seep was screened for soil conductivity. The screening resulted in a measurement of 2.42 mS/cm in a small area. The area of high conductivity was shown to STL Resources Ken Shade. There was about 8 inches of water in northwest stormwater vault. About 12 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in either vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. There has been no pad surface remediation completed. The DEP screened the five seeps and three stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. Infiltration berm 1 along the access road that had a section erode observed on February 18, 2022 has been filled in and compost filter sock has been added near the berm. The other four infiltration berms with erosion noted in Inspection Report 3324293 have been filled in. The infiltration berms along the access road have not been seeded or temporarily stabilized. It appears that earth work on the infiltration berms along the access road has been completed. The DEP recommend seeding and temporarily stabilizing the infiltration berms according to ¿102.22(b). This will help with preventing another situation of sediment discharging outside of the LOD and help prevent accelerated erosion of bare earth. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 6, 7, and 9 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 943719
Permit API: 081-21472
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Eldred Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/31/2022
Comments: On January 31, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at Inflection Energy TLC Well Pad due to a reported spill. Inflection Energy Zac Subra left a message for DEP representative Brad Kline at 1150 explaining that a rented GPU dump had a washout due to a gush of sand causing a leak of production fluid to form. The leak overflowed the containment and impacted an area of snow and pad surface near the southwest corner of the pad. The area of impact was about 25 yards by 10 yards. Conductivity of free standing liquid in the secondary containment for the GPU was over range of the Oakton multimeter. The maximum conductivity range for the meter is 20,000 uS/cm. The well pad surface was screened with a soil conductivity meter and the conductivity ranged from 800 uS/cm to 2,800 uS/cm. The production fluid did not appear to flow off the well pad edge. The operator of the rented GPU noticed the leak on January 30, 2022 but did not notice any breech of containment and reported it to Inflection Energy. Inflection Energy Zac Subra arrived the next morning to follow up and noticed some staining in the snow around the containment for the GPU. Inflection Energy then began to vacuum out the secondary containment and, remove to contaminated ice snow near the GPU. Mr. Subra said the Penn E&R will be out to the well site to delineate the area of impact on February 1, 2022. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. The DEP recommends beginning the Act 2 process due to the unknown volume of the spill.

Inspection Date: 2/01/2024
Comments: On February 1, 2024, inspection conducted at the Athena well pad in Washington Township, Westmoreland County. ESCGP approval was obtained on January 10, 2022 and expires on January 9, 2027. Present were Olympus Energy representative Laura Karosic, independent consultants Brad Latimer and Jeff Leary, and myself. Briefly present was Olympus Energy representative Jim Noon. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that was discovered while removing containment from the pad. The operator reports discovering at least 5 gallons of an oily material on the well pad. The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP, PPC plan, ESCGP approval letter, and E and S inspection logs were onsite (see photos 2-4). However, no E and S inspections beyond November 22, 2023 were available in the log onsite. The access road appeared to be stable with no evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The well pad was excavated at the time of inspection to install flow lines to the newly-drilled Utica wells onsite (see photos 6 and 14). A stained area of approximately 65 feet by 55 feet (according to measurements taken by the operator) was observed on the pad (see photos 7-10). Onsite consultants stated that they attempted to dig into the stained gravel in an attempt to gauge how far down the staining goes, but were unable. Ms. Karosic reported conductivity readings below 1,000 Microsiemens in the stained area. She also reported that the well pad drainages were closed-in upon discovery of the stained area. She informed the DEP that sampling will be conducted and remediation will be handled by Moody and Associates within the coming week, and additional information will be provided as additional discoveries are made in their investigation. The operator anticipates to conduct remediation in accordance with Act 2. Because it is unknown when the secondary containment failed, the DEP inquired on the timeline that it was on the pad. The aforementioned representatives informed the DEP that containment was first placed on the pad in late July of 2023 for drilling of the two Utica wells. Additional containment layers and rig mats were placed approximately six months ago for Completions, and the two Utica wells currently await to be fracked. GPU units onsite are equipped with raised secondary containment skids (see photo 13). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 11). The six additional wells onsite that appear to be in production were equipped with well tags, and did not appear to have any evidence of leaks or discharge on the ground around them at the time of inspection (see photo 15). All other containments onsite that appeared to contain regulated substances were placed in secondary containment. PCSM BMP's appeared to be constructed according to the plans onsite. The Department checked the downslope well pad drainages for any evidence of staining or impact from the newly discovered spill. No staining, distressed vegetation, or anything that would substantiate the occurrence of a recent spill was observed (see photos 5 and 18-25). Before departing from site, the DEP spoke with Olympus representative Jim Noon to inform him that the onsite E and S inspection log was incomplete, and that this has also been observed at another Olympus Pad. He stated that Olympus will conduct additional follow up with their EI's and provide them electronically for this site.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued for releasing this unknown oily substance to the surface of the well pad. An additional violation is being issued for threatening the WOTC, as the ground water depth appears to be shallow at approximately 15-200 centimeters in this area according to surveys conducted by the USDA.

Violation ID: 8286923
Permit API: 117-22075
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/27/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that an estimated 25 gallons of produced fluid was released to the pad surface on August 27, 2026 at 0600. The notification stated that a clamp on the sight glass of a water truck malfunctioned and led to the release of 10 gallons of produced fluid per minute for 2.5 minutes. I met with Mike Deming of Expand Energy upon arriving on location. An area of dark staining was present on the pad surface and a mini-excavator was beginning to scrape up the impacted pad material. The staining covered approximately 100 square feet. The material that the mini-excavator had scraped into piles had an electrical conductivity (EC) of greater than 4 mS/cm as measured by the Hanna Soil Conductivity meter. In the areas of staining that had already had an inch or so of material scraped off, the EC was between 0.14-0.17 mS/cm. A roll-off box was delivered during this inspection and was placed onto secondary containment to containerize the impacted pad material. Representatives from an environmental consultant were also present and said that the EC of the fluid on the surface immediately following the spill was 143 mS/cm. No fluid was observed on the pad surface during this inspection.Mr. Deming stated that they are confident in the release volume estimate based on the flow rate coming out of the truck and the length of time that the release occurred. He stated that they would not pursue Act 2 remediation.Ten wells are staged for production on the well pad. Ten GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. No E and S issues noted. A compressor is also present on the well pad within secondary containment.Violations noted against permit 117-22075.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2020-02-03
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to inspection 2975784 conducted on 12/20/2019 in response to a leak from one of the Production Tanks reported by a PADEP OGI inspector. The Act 9 Sign is present. The Department recommends that the operator maintains the sign to ensure that its contents remain easily visible. The ERP is in the mailbox and is site specific. The site appears constructed and equipped for production with x2 Production Tanks in an earthen dike, x2 separators and the well fenced off. The well is labeled, no leaks, dead or distressed vegetation observed. The Production Tanks are both labeled as "Not In Use." Both appear to be covered in corrosion. No holes visually discernible. The Department advises the operator that they must have the land owners permission to keep such equipment on site, otherwise it should be removed. The impacted area appears to be remediated, with visibly impacted stone removed and replaced. No leaks observed around Production Tanks. There appears to be an animal hole in the earthen dike. The Department recommends that the operator exclude the animal and maintain the dike. No response has been received by the Department in reference to inspection 2975784. As such the Department is again requesting maintenance logs for the Production Tanks and a timeline for when the operator is planning to remove or fix the Production Tanks. Based on this inspection, and no received response on information requested regarding the brine release, all violations will remain open. The Department recommends that the operator monitor the site for distressed vegetation. The Department also requests disposal records and a waste manifest for any contaminated materials removed from the site in response to this release. Further violations may be forthcoming based on responses received by the operator.

Inspection Date: 3/29/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report from the operator that an estimated 20 barrels of a fresh water and produced water mixture had been released to the surface of Pad B on the same day, 3/29/22. I met with EQT representative Rick Hall upon arriving on location. Mr. Hall stated that a frac tank had been overflowed with the produced water and fresh water mixture. He said the fluid had made its way outside of the secondary containment and into the travel lane and ditch along the southwest pad edge. There is a brush barrier alongside the ditch at the edge of the pad. No fluid was observed on the opposite side of the brush barrier. I took several electrical conductivity (EC) readings of the fluid on the pad surface and in the mud in the ditch. With the Oakton conductivity meter I measured an EC of >19.99 on the pad surface immediately next to the edge of the containment where the frac tanks are located. In the middle of the travel lane, I measured an EC of approximately 16 mS/cm. The mud in the ditch at the pad edge gave me an EC reading of approximately 14 mS/cm. Excavators were present on the pad in addition to roll-off boxes to contain excavated material. A Tobias construction crew began to excavate the affected pad material during this inspection. A Creston Environmental employee was also present conducting screening on the pad surface with a YSI meter. On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. No issues noted on Pad A. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation for the release on Pad B due to the estimated volume of the release. The Department requests a justification for the estimated spill volume. Violations noted.

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 949518
Permit API: 081-21885
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/29/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report from the operator that an estimated 20 barrels of a fresh water and produced water mixture had been released to the surface of Pad B on the same day, 3/29/22. I met with EQT representative Rick Hall upon arriving on location. Mr. Hall stated that a frac tank had been overflowed with the produced water and fresh water mixture. He said the fluid had made its way outside of the secondary containment and into the travel lane and ditch along the southwest pad edge. There is a brush barrier alongside the ditch at the edge of the pad. No fluid was observed on the opposite side of the brush barrier. I took several electrical conductivity (EC) readings of the fluid on the pad surface and in the mud in the ditch. With the Oakton conductivity meter I measured an EC of >19.99 on the pad surface immediately next to the edge of the containment where the frac tanks are located. In the middle of the travel lane, I measured an EC of approximately 16 mS/cm. The mud in the ditch at the pad edge gave me an EC reading of approximately 14 mS/cm. Excavators were present on the pad in addition to roll-off boxes to contain excavated material. A Tobias construction crew began to excavate the affected pad material during this inspection. A Creston Environmental employee was also present conducting screening on the pad surface with a YSI meter. On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. No issues noted on Pad A. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation for the release on Pad B due to the estimated volume of the release. The Department requests a justification for the estimated spill volume. Violations noted.

Comments: On May 7, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Cowden 6H gas well located on the Cowden 16 well pad in Hopewell Twp, Washington Co. Due to database error, this inspection report lists the Farm Name and Well # as the Cowden 9H OG Well. Matthew Anderson/Big Dog Energy is reportedly the agent intending to operate the gas wells on the Cowden 16 well pad. According to DEP records, Diversified owns both the gas wells on the pad and the well pad. While on-site, the Department spoke with BDE representatives Matt Kuhn and Chris McNichols, who both were unaware of when the ERP would be available on site. Mr. McNichols prompted Mr. Kuhn call and inquire about the status of the ERP, however, the Department was not made aware of any potential updates regarding the ERP while on-site. Violations are being continued at this time for failure to have the ERP on site.At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that any of the wells at the Cowden well site are in production yet (the 6H, 10H, and 16H). At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a white above ground storage tank on the graveled well pad, the Department did not observe this tank to be connected to gas wells or any other production equipment on the Cowden 16 well pad. Reportedly, this tank is just being stored on the Cowden 16 pad until it could be moved to a different well pad for production use, however, a timeline of when this tank will be removed from the site has yet to be provided to the Department.At the time of this inspection, the Department also observed additional production equipment that did not appear to be connected to any other production equipment or any wells on the well pad. A white structure that was previously observed to be located on site and not connected to any production equipment or wells on the well pad appears to be removed. Violations issued for failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for the production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad are continued at this time as the white structure was the only equipment not in use observed to be removed from the site at this time.On 4/02/2026, the Department received an email from Mr. Anderson, which states "As we stated our ERPs and some signage was stolen We are having new ones written up and sign ordered. The unused equipment will be in use soon."At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed a well tag fixed to the 6H gas well with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the 6H gas well at this time.Based on today's inspection, violations issued to the 6H gas well are to remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: On 8/19/2026 Jason Branan (OGI) notified Caleb Peterson and I about a potential brine release in a farm field off Lebanon Road, Saltsburg, Pa. We went to the site at 9:20 am. There was a black, plastic riser in a field, and there appeared to be brine spilling out onto the ground. We used the soil conductivity probe and tested the release area. The soil conductivity was 6.62 ms/cm. There were no gas wells in view near the riser, but we did observe a pipeline marker for UGI Energy Services nearby. We notified UGI about the spill. We also notified Diversified about the spill because they operate wells nearby. At 2:53 pm, Diversified called and said the release was from a brine transfer line for coalbed methane wells in the area. Caleb and I returned to the release location on 8/20/2026. The riser was no longer filled with brine. The spill area was approximately 60 feet long, and the spill amount is greater than 42-gallons. The closest Diversified coalbed methane well near the spill location is 063-35508.Due to the spill being greater than 42-gallons, the Department is requesting remediation and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Violations are noted below.

Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up after the Department discovered fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC) in the northwest stormwater channel. Two workover rigs are in operation on the well pad. I met with company man Marc McCartor upon arriving on location. He informed me that no excavation had taken place yet in the northwest stormwater channel. He said a sump was installed at the west corner at the end of the stormwater channel. He said that a vacuum truck is on site sucking up the fluid from the channel and the sump. The EC of the fluid in the sump near the halfway point of the northwest pad edge was 333 uS/cm. Farther west, the EC of the fluid in the channel near the location of the sample taken in the previous inspection on 5/8/24 was 798 uS/cm. Farther west within the channel, the EC was 2.34 mS/cm. In the sump at the west corner of the pad within the liner, the EC of the fluid was 2.01 mS/cm. Under the liner, the EC of the fluid was 1600 uS/cm.The Department recommends continuing to collect and dispose of the fluid in the northwest stormwater channel and in the sump. I made this recommendation to the company man before leaving the location. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21946 for the elevated electrical conductivity fluid discovered by the Department in the northwest stormwater channel on 5/8/24.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21938 for the reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface on 3/1/24.
